conventions.convention: n ≥ 2 and integer 1 ≤ r < n; projector matrices are complex Hermitian, satisfy P²=P and tr P=r, and use the real Frobenius pairing Re tr(A*B). Frames are identified under right unitary multiplication.
Whitening uses S=LL*, h=L⁻¹h₀L⁻*, and y=L*c. The interaction G acts on the real Hermitian space and is real-linear and self-adjoint; E_xc is real C² on an open neighborhood of the projector domain.

The density domain consists of Hermitian positive contractions of trace r, with 0<r<n and β>0. Entropy enters with a plus sign as β⁻¹ tr φ(D), where φ(x)=x log x+(1−x)log(1−x), natural logarithms are used, and 0 log 0=0. The energy is real C¹ on an open neighborhood of the full density domain.
Ordered Hermitian eigenvalues are descending, with multiplicity, in the Lipschitz lemma.
The nested sequence starts at K₁. Infima and limits use extended real values, permitting −∞. Equality with the ambient infimum requires the stated energy-recovery property in addition to nestedness.

The commutator is [K,P]=KP−PK; tangent generators K are skew-Hermitian. Stationarity means vanishing of the differential on every projector tangent, without a minimum or eigenvalue-ordering conclusion.
The residual example explicitly assumes Countable Choice when invoking its finite Hermitian residual supplier.

load_bearing.statement: Supply a Hermitian matrix h, a real-linear self-adjoint map G on the real Hermitian space, and a real-valued C² functional E_xc on an open neighborhood of P_r. Define E(P)=tr(hP)+½tr(PG(P))+E_xc(P) and F(P)=h+G(P)+∇E_xc(P).

For n≥2, integer 1≤r<n and β>0, D_r={D∈H_n:0≤D≤I, tr D=r}. With endpoint-extended φ(x)=x log x+(1−x)log(1−x) and a supplied real C¹ energy on an open neighborhood of D_r, define F_β(D)=E(D)+β⁻¹tr φ(D).
For the finite-basis model data, E is real and C² on its stated neighborhood, and for every Hermitian P there and every Hermitian H, DE(P)[H]=tr((h+G(P)+∇E_xc(P))H)=⟨F(P),H⟩_F.

Near P₀, transverse r-dimensional subspaces are uniquely graphs of X:range(P₀)→range(P₀)⊥, with projector P(X)=J_X(I+X*X)⁻¹J_X*. These are open smooth coordinates, and the tangent matrices are exactly the Hermitian off-diagonal blocks. Two orthonormal frames represent the same projector exactly when related by a right unitary matrix.
For 0≺D≺I and every Hermitian direction H, D tr(D log D+(I−D)log(I−D))[H]=tr(H(log D−log(I−D))).
For a C¹ energy on an open neighborhood of D_r, 0<r<n and β>0, every global minimizer of F_β satisfies 0≺D≺I.
A projector P∈P_r is stationary for E restricted to P_r if and only if [F(P),P]=0. Stationarity alone does not assert a minimum.

For nested nonempty compact feasible sets K₁⊆K₂⊆⋯ in K and one continuous real energy E, m_j=min_{K_j}E is nonincreasing and converges, allowing −∞, to inf_{∪K_j}E. The stated energy-recovery property additionally identifies this with inf_K E.

concerns.concern: Facts F1 attributes the improper-integral identity log x=∫₀∞((1+s)⁻¹−(x+s)⁻¹)ds to thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral. That supplier states log′(x)=1/x and log x=∫₁ˣdt/t, rather than the improper-integral representation. Proof 1.1 locally derives the additional identity by finite integration and a limit, so the mathematics closes; the attribution should distinguish the supplied result from this local derivation.

Verification 2.1 says, “The nonzero residual threshold can be zero”. The phrase is contradictory. The verified example has residual norm ρ=0 and correctly demonstrates that zero residual does not identify the lowest eigenvalue; only the wording needs correction.

seams_checked.note: Checked the whitening and finite Hermitian residual suppliers against their consuming definition and examples. S=LL*, h=L⁻¹h₀L⁻*, y=L*c and quotient preservation agree exactly. The residual example retains Countable Choice and imports spectral proximity without claiming ground-state identification.

The optimization example uses the Riemannian method's Cauchy fallback with B=0. Checked the underlying Cauchy-decrease bound and its small-radius use in real tangent coordinates. The consumer makes no cubic-regularization, second-order or inner-operation complexity claim.

Checked complex quotient conventions, horizontal projections, projector gradient, polar retraction, algorithm and first-order complexity theorem. The example uses the real Frobenius metric, gradient 2(I−P)F(P)X, a globally defined horizontal polar map, B=0 and a sufficient outer cap. Its compact bounded tangent-disk argument supplies uniform pullback-gradient Lipschitzness. The O(ε⁻²) claim concerns accepted and rejected outer trials.

Checked the response-map definition, gapped-projector well-definedness, admissible-density inclusion and mixing, block-projector derivative, level-shift equivalence, and finite-model C¹-response corollary. They preserve the Hermitian rank-r projector domain and the model's open-domain C² hypothesis. Ascending eigenvalue order is explicitly fixed for the lowest-r response. A positive gap supplies local projector regularity, without importing contraction or minimum claims.
